findings.title: Inverted condition and wrong substring indices in isAccessTokenId matcher
findings.body:
In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut)`, the check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` has two bugs:
1. The prefix before `:` is 6 characters long (`<2-char sessionType><2-char tokenType><2-char grantType>`), so the grant type shortcut is at indices `(4, 6)` (matching `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId`), not `(3, 5)`.
2. The equality check is not negated: it returns `false` when the substring equals `expectedGrantShortcut` and `true` when it does not. Because `substring(3, 5)` extracts the second character of the token type plus the first character of the grant type (e.g. `"ta"` for `"onrtac"`), it never equals `"ac"`, causing the assertion to accidentally pass for any grant shortcut (and it would also throw `IndexOutOfBoundsException` if `items[0]` has fewer than 5 characters).

findings.title: Constructor checks grantType for null twice instead of checking rawTokenId
findings.body: In the `AccessTokenContext` constructor, line 73 calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. Passing a null `rawTokenId` will therefore not be rejected as intended.

findings.title: Javadoc on OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() says 3-letters shortcut
findings.body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` documents the return value as "usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants", whereas `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` strictly requires the grant shortcut to be 2 characters long (expecting a total prefix length of 6 characters and slicing `encodedContext.substring(4, 6)`). Implementing a custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` with a 3-letter shortcut as suggested by the Javadoc will cause `getTokenContextFromTokenId` to fail with `IllegalArgumentException: Incorrect token id ... Expected length of 6`.
